items.title: SPX iron condor fills average $0.15–$0.25 below displayed mid price
items.summary: The author tracked 60 SPX iron condor fills against displayed mid prices and found consistent fill execution at $0.15–$0.25 below the displayed mid on 4-leg spreads showing a mid of approximately $2.80, accounting for a 15–20% gap between modeled and realized returns. The author states the discrepancy was persistent across 50–60 iron condors and was not resolved by adjusting strikes, DTE, or delta targets on the short legs.
items.relevance_to_sofar: Agent assessment: This is directly actionable for SOFAR's prediction backchecking and signal attribution module. A systematic $0.15–$0.25 mid-to-fill gap on SPX iron condors is a calibration input for SOFAR's backtest fill assumptions — if SOFAR models fills at mid, realized P&L will persistently underperform projections. The finding also has implications for SOFAR's GEX-driven trade setup evaluation and 3D scoring feedback loop.

items.summary: The article describes a momentum strategy applied to 2-year Treasury notes, premised on the observation that FOMC policy moves in long, persistent cycles of multi-year hikes or cuts rather than frequent reversals.
